title: Middleware: logging, panic recovery, CORS and authentication

videos.script: Lesson 1 left boxoffice answering requests. Nothing records them, a bug kills the reply, and anyone can call anything. {{wrap}} This lesson fixes all three without touching a handler. The tool is a middleware: a handler that holds another handler. {{order}} It does its part, calls the one inside, and can act again on the way out. Wrap two of them and the order matters, so you will watch it happen. {{log}} The first one logs every request. The hard part is the status code, because a response writer never tells you what was sent. So you hand the handler a writer that remembers. {{panic}} Then a panic. You will see what net/http does with one by itself, and why the client deserves a 500 instead. {{cors}} Then CORS, from the server's side. It does not protect the server, and the transcript proves it. {{auth}} Last, a token check on the staff routes only, and the difference between 401 and 403.
